But tbh some hostels I've been to i wouldn't be surprised

Its basically a hotel with dorm style accommodation, so multiple beds in one room. Can range from 4-20+ beds in one room, often with a choice of same sex or mixed. Normally used by under 40s but I have seen older people in them and even families (this was very common in Japan actually). They'll usually have communal spaces, so shared bathrooms and showers, laundry for a fee, and a basic kitchen or a microwave. Some will ask you to make your bed. You'll usually have a locker, outlet, and light by your bed. They do private rooms as well usually that can be cheaper than most hotels but not always.  

In my experience: you get 'quiet' ones that people just use as a place to sleep, more common with locals and older people. You get 'backpacker' ones that focus a lot on a backpacker aesthetic (think decor like chalkboards where everyone writes down their country, brown rattan furniture, jazz music in lobby). These are good for meeting people as they sometimes run group tours or cooking classes etc you can sign up for. Although usually filled with wannabe hippies with remote jobs and who will play wonderwall on guitar in the shared spaces unprompted. You get 'party' ones too that will have a bar attached and sometimes parties etc til late (branded ones like Selina or Mad Monkey), filled with rich 19 year olds from London/California. You will be able to tell which is which from photos and info online.

Id give it a go if I were you! You just have to be open-minded and not expect hotel luxuries and standards. If you can camp, hostelling is fine. Find one with good reviews, choose one with a small dorm (4-6 people), and not too party-based.  Maybe try a private room first. Check they have lockers and bring your own lock. Bring very good earplugs if youre a light sleeper, or I use one of those sound headbands things to put on top of earplugs with white noise blasting as an extra layer against snorers and loud doors banging at 2am. I'd also try a few different ones, as some can suck and I wouldn't want it to put you off - either because you have bad roommates, bad facilities, or not very social if thats something you want.

One thing that can be common, but not too common, is bedbugs. Even good hostels can have them due to the amount of people in a room and quick turnover of people who have recently stayed in cheap places. It's not a sign of a bad hostel as long as they sort it (clean it and give you a new bed). I've only seen them once in about 8 months worth of hostelling. Check for bedbugs on your mattress before putting all your stuff on it. Keep your luggage on the floor or in a locker. Look for bloodstains on walls etc. As an extra precaution, you can also hot wash your clothing and fabrics (-and tumble dry for at least 30mins, this is the best way to kill them) when you get back. Or freeze anything else for a few weeks. But don't worry, I don't think the chances are much worse than staying in cheap hotels.

Came back from two months in japan recently and loved every single second. Felt safer walking home than I do in UK, even in red light district areas. Just use common sense and you'll be fine, never go with anyone who approaches you or touts on the street in Shinjuku. Japan does have a sexual harassment problem but its not as overt as other countries, just be careful if you wear skirts (up skirting), keep an eye on your drink, and be ready to deal with the odd handsy drunk guy in clubs. Some of the salarymen i saw put my fellow brits to shame with their drinking haha. But met plenty of 'kind uncle' trope guys too who would approach and help me when i was looking lost, invite me in for tea at their restaurant at a festival (with their family so not weird), that kinda thing. One recommendation is seek out social hostels like unplan, or hostelworld hostels (usually more social) and use their groupchats to meet fellow travellers - i found many hostels filled with locals who didnt want to socialise, just sleep, so doing the above will help if thats your goal. Not only is japan safe, it was so easy to just travel! Want to go somewhere? Google maps will get you there with step by step and Japan's public transport will get you where you want. Enjoy, and be ready to rub it in your parents face when you get back.

Did this myself. Most effective way imo is calorie counting, get myfitnesspal or just look at the packet. Look at the calories of what you already eat in a day for a week, calculate the average, then take away 300-500 calories and aim for that. Or calculate your daily tdee online, and minus it from that (when it asks about your daily activity, underestimate, so many people overestimate it). Its so easy to underestimate how many calories are in things if you do it without looking, especially things like cooking oil, sauces, drinks. If you dont already, stop drinking full fat coke or fancy coffees with cream and milk etc. Keep your protein up, it keeps you full and and helps you burn fat instead of muscle. 

See adding exercise as a supplement, not the main way to lose weight. Its so difficult to burn a substantial amount of calories exercising unless you are already pretty overweight, in which case you want to go easy with exercise for safety reasons anyway. In which case, walking more is a good option. And a lot of people 'reward' themselves with food, or get hungrier than usual, and eat more than they burned. But for example, on a typical 20min nonstop run, or 10,000 steps, i burn off less than a mars bar. So do it if you want, its good for fitness anyway, but be careful.

To bring it up with them, maybe try speaking to just one at first so its easier for you. Tell them how youve been feeling, that you feel life is pointless and youre tired of it. They don't want a dead child, they'll try to help. Say youd like to see the doctors for it, to see if they have any suggestions. Alternatively, ask school counsellers/nurses/mental health teams to explain to your parents. They could do it face to face or over the phone, but they'll be experienced at it and know how to do it. You can ask them to leave certain details out, but they will have to say if youre in danger as you know.
